text:
San Jose had gone five games without a win, and it took eight rounds of a shootout to end it. Ivar Stenberg, who had tied the game in the first period, beat Ilya Sorokin on the last shot, and the Sharks edged the Islanders 3-2 after both teams scored twice in regulation and nothing in overtime.

The result flattered New York less than the scoreboard suggests. By expected goals, which measure the quality of the chances each side created, San Jose led 4.12 to 3.29, and the Sharks took 68 shot attempts to 56. Our simulations of every shot give San Jose a 62 percent chance of deserving the win. The Islanders were kept in it by Sorokin, a goalie drafted 78th overall in 2014 who stopped 37 of 39 shots. That was about two goals better than the chances he faced would normally allow. Macklin Celebrini's 34 percent look in overtime was the best one he turned away.

The goals traded evenly. Ben Hutton opened the scoring, Stenberg answered, Victor Eklund put the Islanders back ahead on the power play, and Tyler Toffoli tied it with a slap shot in the second. Yaroslav Askarov, drafted 11th overall by Nashville in 2020, made 30 saves for the Sharks and was named first star. The win ends the 0-5-0 slide. The Islanders are 0-2-2 over their last four and still looking for a win.
